alerts.title: Fresh landslide near Jangalikh village (Rohru, Chhohara block) blocks pedestrian route on Sundru Khad
alerts.summary: A fresh landslide near Jangalikh village in Chhohara development block of Rohru sub-division, Shimla district, sent debris into the Sundru Khad on 28 September, blocking the pedestrian route to the village. The Rohru SDM confirmed that despite fears of a temporary blockage forming a lake in the khad, water flow has returned to normal and no lake formed; the administration is continuing to monitor the site.
alerts.impact: Treat the Jangalikh (Chhohara block, Rohru) pedestrian/foot route as non-serviceable for FM pickups until debris is cleared; vehicular LM in the wider Rohru belt is unaffected for now since the khad did not dam up, but keep a short watch for renewed slippage given the string of active slides elsewhere in Shimla and Mandi districts this week.

alerts.title: Rockfall shuts Badrinath-Rishikesh NH at Sirobagarh (Pauri Garhwal); pilgrim and goods traffic stranded both sides
alerts.summary: Heavy two-day rain triggered fresh rockfall/debris at the Sirobagarh stretch (Pauri Garhwal) on Sep 27, burying the Badrinath-Rishikesh NH and stranding pilgrim traffic on both sides. As of Sep 28 authorities have given no reopening timeline and are advising vehicles to halt at safe points; the IMD-driven Char Dham Yatra suspension issued with the Sep 26-27 red alert remains in effect, with conditions expected to ease only from Sep 29.
alerts.impact: Treat the Rishikesh-Badrinath/Joshimath corridor as non-serviceable for LM/FM until clearance is confirmed; hold shipments at Rishikesh/Srinagar(UK) hub and expect improvement only from Sep 29 onward per IMD.

alerts.title: Mayurbhanj: 20 blocks flooded, 10,373 people relocated; Betnoti-Badasahi and Manatri-Baisinga roads cut
alerts.summary: Flooding across Mayurbhanj district has affected 20 blocks plus one municipality and one Notified Area Council, with 10,373 people relocated to 89 relief camps and 72 free-kitchen centres running; three ODRAF and 18 fire-service teams are deployed. The Betnoti-Badasahi and Manatri-Baisinga roads are blocked, and the Budhabalanga river is running 2-3 feet over the Nakhara bridge in Betnoti block, affecting Patalipura and Kalama villages (Betnoti) and Salagaon, Managobindapur, Chandanpur, Durgapur, Kendudiha and Balabhadrapur (Badasahi). Schools are shut in Thakurmunda, Kaptipada, Udala, Gopabandhunagar, Khunta, Badasahi and Betnoti blocks, though Udala, Kaptipada, Bangiriposi and Saraskana are showing recession and reopening roads.
alerts.impact: Flag Betnoti and Badasahi block pincodes as non-serviceable while the Betnoti-Badasahi and Manatri-Baisinga roads stay cut; hold FM pickups from these blocks and route Baripada-hub line-haul via alternate roads. Udala, Kaptipada, Bangiriposi and Saraskana pincodes can resume normal SLA as roads reopen there.

alerts.title: Khordha: flood-like situation in Banpur, Banpur-Balugaon road cut off, paddy fields inundated
alerts.summary: Heavy rainfall has triggered a flood-like situation in Banpur block of Khordha district, with floodwater entering residential areas and the Banpur-Balugaon road submerged and disconnected. Paddy fields around Banpur are inundated, affecting local farmers, as the wider Khordha-Puri coastal belt remains under the influence of the weakening Bay of Bengal depression.
alerts.impact: Flag Banpur block pincodes (Khordha district) as non-serviceable for LM/FM until the Banpur-Balugaon road reopens; reroute Khordha-Puri coastal linehaul via NH-16 and hold rural pickups in the Banpur belt.

alerts.title: Hirakud Dam opens up to 20 gates as Mahanadi rises; Sambalpur-Subarnapur-Baragarh and delta districts on watch
alerts.summary: Hirakud Dam authorities have been progressively closing sluice gates as reservoir water levels decline (ommcomnews reports gates down to single digits from a peak of 28-30 open). At Mundali on the Mahanadi delta, inflow was 7.60 lakh cusecs as of Sep28 morning, still below the 10 lakh cusecs threshold considered a danger zone, per Odisha govt/Minister Suresh Pujari.
alerts.impact: Delta flood risk is easing but not eliminated; Mahanadi is still rising, not yet a declared danger zone. FM/LM routes through Cuttack/Jagatsinghpur/Kendrapara delta belt should stay on watch but de-escalate from critical planning.

alerts.title: Fagudoba village on Sankosh river (Bengal-Bhutan-Assam border) losing land to erosion, SSB camp at risk
alerts.summary: Fagudoba, one of the last settlements on the West Bengal-Bhutan and West Bengal-Assam border, is losing farmland and forest to erosion by the Sankosh river, which originates in Bhutan. Heavy siltation and debris flow from Bhutan have raised the riverbed, and the eroding bank now threatens an SSB (Sashastra Seema Bal) camp on the India-Bhutan border in addition to village land.
alerts.impact: Flag Fagudoba and other Sankosh-riverside border villages for extended TAT and hold FM pickups from sellers there; monitor for a full village cut-off if erosion accelerates through the tail of the monsoon.

alerts.title: Balasore: Subarnarekha and Jalaka above danger mark, 154+ villages flooded across Bhograi, Baliapal, Jaleswar, Basta
alerts.summary: OdishaTV (Sep27) reports Subarnarekha water level is falling in Balasore but the flood situation 'remains grim' with many villages still marooned; statewide update (Sep28) confirms Subarnarekha is among the rivers now receding.
alerts.impact: Trend is improving but village-level marooning and crop damage continue in Jaleswar/Balasore belt; keep last-mile routes on alert for a few more days before assuming full clearance.

alerts.title: Kharun river floods Amleshwar and Khudmuda villages in Durg; Mahadev Ghat road linking Raipur-Patan-Durg submerged
alerts.summary: Continuous rainfall over the past 24 hours has pushed the Kharun river out of its banks, causing waterlogging in riverside villages across Raipur and Durg districts. The Raipur-Patan-Durg road via Mahadev Ghat is submerged and impassable, and flood-like conditions have been reported in Amleshwar and Khudmuda villages of Durg district, where roads are no longer visible under floodwater and water has entered homes. The Raipur-Bhilai road via Mahadev Ghat is also disrupted by the strong water flow.
alerts.impact: Avoid the Mahadev Ghat route between Raipur, Patan and Durg/Bhilai until water recedes; reroute Raipur-Durg-Bhilai line-haul via NH-53/NH-130 instead. Flag Amleshwar and Khudmuda (Durg district) pincodes for extended TAT and hold FM pickups from riverside sellers there.

alerts.title: Mandya: farmers briefly block Bengaluru-Mysuru highway at Jayachamaraja Wadiyar Circle over Cauvery release to Tamil Nadu
alerts.summary: Raitha Sangha, Karnataka Rakshana Vedike and BJP members protested near Jayachamaraja Wadiyar Circle in Mandya on 25 September against the CWRC/CWMA direction to release 4,000 cusecs of Cauvery water daily to Tamil Nadu for 15 days, briefly blocking the Bengaluru-Mysuru highway. KRS reservoir stood at 105.7 ft against a maximum of 124.8 ft, with farmer leaders warning Karnataka cannot spare more water. CM D K Shivakumar has said the state will challenge the CWRC direction. This dispute continues into the 26 September Bengaluru bandh.
alerts.impact: Treat the Bengaluru-Mysuru highway near Mandya (Jayachamaraja Wadiyar Circle) as intermittently blockable with little notice while the Cauvery dispute runs hot - keep an alternate Bengaluru-Mysuru routing option live for line-haul and avoid scheduling tight-window linehaul through Mandya town during protest hours.

alerts.title: J&K govt tally: 24,416 houses and 5,373 roads damaged in 2025-26/2026-27 floods, Udhampur and Rajouri worst-hit
alerts.summary: J&K government's assembly disclosure puts cumulative 2025-27 cloudburst/flash-flood damage at 24,416 houses, 3,959 roads and 5,597 water-supply schemes. Jammu division accounts for ~95% of the damage (Jammu district alone: 1,692 roads and 3,063 water schemes hit; Udhampur and Rajouri also severe; Ramban has the highest crop loss at 33,780 hectares). 2025-26 damage has been temporarily restored with permanent works ongoing; 2026-27 damage is only partially restored.
alerts.impact: Continue treating Jammu division rural link roads (Jammu, Udhampur, Rajouri, Ramban districts) as higher-risk for delivery delays — permanent restoration is still months out — rather than flagging all of J&K uniformly.

alerts.title: Uttarakhand red alert: Bageshwar, Nainital, Pithoragarh on Sep 26; Dehradun, Haridwar on Sep 27 as western disturbance moves in
alerts.summary: The Sep 26-27 red/orange alert verified out with real impact: Char Dham Yatra was suspended, and rain (amplified by ex-Cyclone Arnab moisture) killed 10 and injured 17 in rain-related incidents across UP overall, including 6 deaths specifically in Lakhimpur Kheri, Amethi and Barabanki. In Pithoragarh, 11 roads were closed district-wide and the Adi Kailash Yatra was halted. IMD indicates conditions easing only from Sep 29.
alerts.impact: Keep elevated SLA buffers and non-serviceable flags for Bageshwar/Nainital/Pithoragarh/Dehradun/Haridwar hubs through Sep 28; reassess for normalization from Sep 29 once the forecast easing materializes.

alerts.title: Himachal Pradesh braces for fresh rain spell Sep 26-29, adding to already-damaged hill roads
alerts.summary: IMD's Sep 26-29 rain spell for Himachal is materializing as forecast, with rain continuing statewide even as the season's monsoon total runs ~13% below normal; Kinnaur recorded its first snowfall of the season at higher elevations.
alerts.impact: No change to guidance — maintain buffer stock and flexible SLAs at Shimla/Mandi/Kullu/Kangra hubs through Sep 29; re-verify road-closure counts once the spell ends.

alerts.title: Two spans of Pamuleru stream bridge near Rajupeta (Mulakalapalli mandal) washed away — Palvoncha–Mandalapalli traffic halted
alerts.summary: Floodwaters in the Pamuleru stream washed away two spans of the bridge near Rajupeta in Mulakalapalli mandal of Bhadradri Kothagudem district, completely stopping traffic between Palvoncha and Mandalapalli. Kothagudem is among five Telangana districts under a red alert until 26 Sep, so restoration is unlikely in the short term.
alerts.impact: Mark Mulakalapalli-mandal villages reachable only via Palvoncha–Mandalapalli as temporarily non-serviceable; reroute Palvoncha/Kothagudem LM via longer alternate roads with a 1-2 day SLA buffer. Hold FM pickups from sellers in the mandal until an alternate route is confirmed.

alerts.title: Kattaleru stream in spate cuts off 20 villages between Vinagadapa and Thotamoola; flash floods across NTR district
alerts.summary: The overflowing Kattaleru stream cut off road access to about 20 villages between Vinagadapa and Thotamoola in NTR district. NewsMeter reported flash floods at several locations in NTR district, with streams and canals overflowing onto major roads and a car carrying a local cooperative society president and his wife swept away. Vijayawada's low-lying areas are waterlogged and paddy between Vijayawada and Rajahmundry is submerged; more heavy rain is forecast for NTR, Krishna, Guntur, Bapatla, Palnadu and Prakasam on 25 Sep.
alerts.impact: Flag the Vinagadapa–Thotamoola cluster (Gampalagudem/Tiruvuru side of NTR district) as non-serviceable until the stream recedes; add 24-48h buffer to Vijayawada rural LM and avoid causeway routes. Watch Vijayawada hub inbound linehauls on 25 Sep.

alerts.title: Floodwater enters Anakapalli RTC complex and railway bridge; Vizag's Tulasi Nagar logs 236 mm, Gajuwaka low-lying areas inundated
alerts.summary: Andhra Pradesh recorded 100 mm+ rain at 80 locations in 24 hours, led by Visakhapatnam Rural's Tulasi Nagar (236 mm), Madhurawada (218 mm) and Seethammadhara (205 mm). Floodwater entered the Anakapalli RTC bus complex and the railway bridge area, and strong winds uprooted 74 electric poles and damaged 50 houses at Chintalapadu. Visakhapatnam MLA Palla Srinivasa Rao toured flood-hit parts of Gajuwaka on 24 Sep.
alerts.impact: Expect 24-48h delays at Visakhapatnam and Anakapalli LM hubs (Madhurawada, Gajuwaka, Anakapalli town pincodes); stagger FM pickups from Vizag industrial sellers and confirm power at sort centres. Avoid underpasses and the Anakapalli railway-bridge stretch for linehaul.

alerts.title: Koraput's Dasmantpur block: 3 ft of water over Damjodi bridge (Nandigaon GP); Haridaphut bridge under water, ~20 villages hit
alerts.summary: In Dasmantpur block of Koraput, about three feet of water was flowing over the bridge near Damjodi village under Nandigaon panchayat, stranding vehicles on both sides. Water also accumulated over the bridge near Haridaphut under Pindapadar panchayat, on the road linking Dasmantpur police-station square with Adimunda square — the lifeline for about 20 villages of Pindapadar and Duarashuni panchayats to Koraput market. Koraput remained under red warning to 25 Sep and the collector has shut all schools and anganwadis on 25 Sep. In Koraput's Kotpad block, heavy rain has also damaged over 100 houses, per district reports on Sep 26.
alerts.impact: Hold LM to Pindapadar/Duarashuni/Nandigaon GP villages (Dasmantpur block) until water recedes; the Dasmantpur–Adimunda road is the only route. Add 48h SLA buffer to Koraput district and expect FM delays for Jeypore/Koraput sellers.

alerts.title: NHAI bars heavy vehicles on Kanpur's Jajmau Ganga bridge for repairs; Lucknow–Kanpur traffic diverted via Ganga Barrage till 13 Dec
alerts.summary: NHAI has stopped heavy-vehicle movement on the Jajmau Ganga bridge in Kanpur for repair work. UPSRTC buses from Lucknow no longer go from the Unnao bypass straight to Jajmau; they now run via Marhla chauraha, Saraiyan crossing and the Ganga Barrage to Jhakarkati, adding about 15 km (fare raised from Rs 123 to Rs 145). The diversion is to remain in force until 13 December.
alerts.impact: Lucknow–Kanpur linehauls and Unnao-side FM milk runs should plan on the Ganga Barrage route (+15 km, extra congestion) until mid-December; re-baseline Kanpur hub cut-off times and inform carriers' Unnao/Jajmau LM teams. Heavy trucks may face slow-downs around Company Bagh/GT Road.

alerts.title: Mangtabong village landslide in Yuksom hits 12 households; NH-10 at 20th Mile Bardang reopened only for one-way traffic
alerts.summary: NH-10's Bardang 20th Mile stretch remains closed/restricted to one-way traffic as of late September 2026, per a Northeast Live TV road-status roundup ('Most Routes Open Amid Monsoon, NH-10's Bardang Stretch Still Closed, Alternate Route Operational') and Borok Times ('NH-10 20th Mile One-Way Traffic Continues Near Bardang'). No confirmation yet of full reopening.
alerts.impact: Continue routing LM/FM linehaul via the alternate route around Bardang; expect one-way convoy timing delays on NH-10 near 20th Mile for Gangtok-bound and Siliguri-bound loads.

alerts.title: Orange alert for Darjeeling, Jalpaiguri, Alipurduar on 25 Sep; high tides spill into Mandarmani, fishing banned off Digha
alerts.summary: The weather office forecast heavy to very heavy rain in North Bengal and Sikkim on 24-25 Sep, with Darjeeling, Jalpaiguri and Alipurduar on orange alert for 25 Sep and a raised risk of landslides and road blockages on NH-10. On the coast, gusty winds hit Digha and Mandarmani, the sea spilled into parts of Mandarmani, and fishermen are barred from going to sea along Digha, Shankarpur, Junput and Petuaghat. Kansabati Dam in Bankura logged 100 mm in 24 hours.
alerts.impact: Watch Siliguri–Darjeeling/Kalimpong and Dooars (Jalpaiguri, Alipurduar) LM on 25 Sep for landslip or waterlogging delays ahead of the Puja volume ramp-up; keep East Midnapore coastal pincodes (Digha, Ramnagar, Contai) on a 24h buffer.

alerts.title: Gangtok: odd-even vehicle curbs on NH-10 Ranipool (Mayfair Jn)–Zero Point stretch under HC-ordered review
alerts.summary: Sikkim High Court on Sep 24, 2026 gave the state government three weeks to revisit/review the NH-10 odd-even vehicle restriction policy around Gangtok/Ranipool, per multiple outlets (ANI, Northeast Live TV, Kalinga TV, The News Mill). The odd-even restriction remains in force pending that review.
alerts.impact: Until the policy changes, LM vehicles in Gangtok town can ply the Ranipool–Zero Point NH-10 stretch only on permitted days — plan alternate-day vehicle rostering (odd/even plates) for Gangtok hubs and keep two-wheeler riders on the core town beats; review again after the Oct 15 hearing.

alerts.title: Malappuram: Kottappuzha flash flood at TK Colony, Pookkottumpadam — one dead, seven feared missing
alerts.summary: The Kottappuzha flash flood near Pookkottumpadam and TK Colony in Malappuram has claimed at least 6 lives as of the latest recovery operations, with search and relief work continuing in the affected stretch.
alerts.impact: Search-and-rescue is complete, so the acute LM stoppage has eased; keep a lighter SLA buffer for Pookkottumpadam/Nilambur hill-foot pincodes during any further heavy afternoon showers, and continue avoiding riverside village roads near Kottappuzha as a standing precaution given the terrain's flash-flood history.

alerts.title: Alluri Sitarama Raju: landslide at Chintalamma Ghat (Koyyuru mandal) drops debris on NH; Araku ghat landslips
alerts.summary: At Chintalamma Ghat Road in Koyyuru mandal of Alluri Sitarama Raju district, parts of the hillside gave way after heavy rain and earth and debris fell onto the National Highway, disrupting traffic on the ghat stretch. Araku Valley has had three days of continuous rain, with landslips reported along several ghat roads. Separately, flash floods hit several places in NTR district as streams and canals overflowed onto major roads, and hundreds of acres of paddy between Vijayawada and Rajahmundry are submerged.
alerts.impact: Avoid Chintalamma Ghat and Araku ghat roads for Vizag-Paderu/Araku feeder runs; move ASR-district LM to daylight-only with a 24-48h SLA buffer and flag Koyyuru, Paderu and Araku pincodes for extended TAT. Expect FM pickup misses in NTR district (Vijayawada rural) where flash floods have reached roads; heavy rain is forecast again on 25 September for NTR, Krishna, Guntur, Bapatla, Palnadu and Prakasam.

alerts.title: Kalahandi: red warning; landslide vigil at Madanpur Rampur, Koksara, Lanjigarh, Thuamul Rampur; Hati and Tel rising
alerts.summary: With IMD's red warning for extremely heavy rain over Kalahandi, Nabarangpur, Koraput and Malkangiri, the Kalahandi administration is maintaining strict vigilance in landslide-prone Madanpur Rampur, Koksara, Lanjigarh and Thuamul Rampur blocks. Continuous rain and gusty winds hit Dharmagada, Koksara and Jaipatna overnight, and the Hati and Tel rivers are steadily rising, prompting warnings to riverside residents. Schools and colleges in Kalahandi are closed; 28 temporary shelters and 13 mobile health units are ready.
alerts.impact: Early-warning item for Kalahandi: pre-flag Thuamul Rampur and Lanjigarh hill pincodes and Hati/Tel riverside villages (Dharmagada, Jaipatna, Koksara) for extended TAT on 24-26 September, and keep Bhawanipatna hub line-haul on main roads only. Escalate to non-serviceable if slides or river overtopping are reported.

alerts.title: Malkangiri: ghat landslide at Bayapada cuts off 18 villages; movement restricted both sides
alerts.summary: Deep-depression rain triggered a landslide on Thursday in the Bayapada area of Malkangiri district, where soil and debris from the ghat slid onto the road and cut off connectivity to 18 villages. Movement has been restricted on both sides of the ghat while the administration clears mud and stones; landslides at multiple other locations in Malkangiri were also reported. In neighbouring Rayagada, knee-deep water accumulated on roads and the Collector has flagged 11 landslide-prone hotspots.
alerts.impact: Treat Bayapada-ghat-dependent villages of Malkangiri as temporarily non-serviceable for LM until the road is cleared; hold FM pickups and route Malkangiri-bound loads with a 24-48h SLA buffer. Watch Rayagada's 11 flagged hotspots before dispatching line-haul through the ghats.

alerts.title: South Odisha: 237 villages in 6 districts hit, 8,082 shifted; bridges near Damjodi and Haridaphut under water
alerts.summary: Statewide picture has grown since Sep24: OdishaTV (Sep28) reports 26 districts, 7,834 villages across 1,360 gram panchayats/205 blocks, and 219 urban wards in 38 ULBs affected in total, with over 1 lakh people moved to relief camps (PTI, Sep27). Minister Suresh Pujari says situation should improve over the next 24 hours as Subarnarekha, Baitarani, Salandi and Budhabalanga levels decline.
alerts.impact: Still a state-scale disruption for LM/FM across south and coastal Odisha; plan for continued village-level cut-offs through at least Sep29 even as the overall trend turns towards improvement.

alerts.title: Keonjhar: water flowing over Panga and Sankarpur bridges in Telkoi, traffic hit
alerts.summary: Water is flowing over the Panga and Sankarpur bridges in Telkoi block of Keonjhar district, affecting traffic in the area, as the deep-depression rain spreads north from south Odisha. Telkoi's bridge crossings have repeatedly overtopped this monsoon, cutting links toward Jagamohanpur and NH-49.
alerts.impact: Hold LM vans for Telkoi-block villages beyond the Panga/Sankarpur crossings until water recedes; route Keonjhar-bound loads via NH-20/NH-49 main corridors and expect 1-day delay for Telkoi pincodes.

alerts.title: Andhra: 613 km of R&B roads damaged by deep depression, 356 km in Srikakulam alone; 4 washouts
alerts.summary: R&B Minister B.C. Janardhan Reddy said 613 km of state roads were damaged as of 7 a.m. Thursday, with Srikakulam accounting for 356 km. Roads were washed away at four locations by deep craters, cross-drainage works damaged at 78 locations (37 under restoration), and traffic disrupted at 23 locations (14 cleared). Damage is spread across Srikakulam, Parvathipuram-Manyam, Vizianagaram, Alluri Sitarama Raju, Visakhapatnam, Anakapalli, Kakinada, East Godavari, Konaseema, West Godavari, Anantapur, Kurnool and Nandyal.
alerts.impact: Srikakulam, Parvathipuram-Manyam and Vizianagaram LM should run on a 24-48h SLA buffer with alternate routing around washed-out stretches; watch Vizag hub outbound to north-coastal pincodes. 614 accident-prone spots have been flagged — avoid night line-haul on ghat and CD-damaged sections.

alerts.title: Vijayawada: continuous rain floods low-lying areas as deep depression moves inland
alerts.summary: After the deep depression crossed near Kalingapatnam between 11 pm Sep 23 and 1 am Sep 24, continuous rain since Thursday morning flooded low-lying areas of Vijayawada. IMD expects the system to hold deep-depression intensity for about 12 hours before weakening while moving north-northwest.
alerts.impact: Vijayawada city LM (low-lying colonies) may see failed attempts and slower first-attempt delivery today; keep Vijayawada/NTR district FM pickups flexible and watch for Krishna-district waterlogging spillover into Friday.

alerts.title: Telangana: Jayashankar Bhupalpally drenched as deep depression rain washes away roads, submerges crops
alerts.summary: Roads in Jayashankar Bhupalpally district remain washed out and submerged crop fields have been confirmed damaged, with the swelling Godavari specifically flagged as having damaged chilli crops in the district (Deccan Chronicle).
alerts.impact: Expect LM delays for interior Bhupalpally mandal pincodes and possible FM pickup gaps; route Bhupalpally-bound loads via main state highways only and add a 24h SLA buffer until road damage is assessed.

alerts.title: Srikakulam: Vamsadhara and Nagavali in spate; culvert at Gangavaram washed away, 53 riverside villages on alert
alerts.summary: The Vamsadhara and Nagavali rivers in Srikakulam district are in spate with heavy inflows after the deep depression's landfall. A canal culvert at Gangavaram village was washed away, cutting road links to several villages, and precautionary measures are in place in 53 villages in the river basin. The district red alert continues, with cyclone-impact risk flagged in ten coastal mandals; rainwater entered homes at Bhavani Nagar in Tekkali and a tree fell in Neelapuram mandal.
alerts.impact: Flag villages beyond the Gangavaram culvert and low-lying Vamsadhara-Nagavali basin pincodes as non-serviceable until the road is restored. Hold Srikakulam and Tekkali LM for 24-25 September and reroute via NH-16 only once waters drop.

alerts.title: Odisha: huge rock blocks Paribeta Ghat road in Gajapati's R. Udayagiri block; 1,500 evacuated statewide
alerts.summary: Incessant rain triggered a landslide on the Paribeta Ghat road in R. Udayagiri block of Gajapati district, where a huge rock tumbled onto the road and disrupted traffic; no injuries were reported. Gajapati has identified 140 landslide-vulnerable spots. Across south Odisha, falling trees and road blockades have been reported from Gajapati and Ganjam, with about 1,500 people evacuated and rainfall of around 230 mm recorded.
alerts.impact: Treat R. Udayagiri and Mohana-side Gajapati pincodes as extended-TAT until the ghat is cleared; avoid Paribeta Ghat for Berhampur-Paralakhemundi feeder runs. Keep Ganjam and Gajapati FM pickups on hold for 24 September.

alerts.title: Assam: Brahmaputra within 10 m of breaching Biswanath Ghat-Panpur embankment at Solmari village
alerts.summary: Assam Tribune reports the Brahmaputra has come within roughly 10 metres of breaching the Biswanath–Panpur embankment near Solmari, with Sentinel Assam separately reporting continued erosion panic among residents in the area. Breach risk is heightened, not resolved.
alerts.impact: Early-warning item for Biswanath district: an embankment breach would flood Biswanath Ghat and Panpur-side villages. Keep Biswanath Chariali LM on normal SLA but pre-flag riverside pincodes for extended TAT, and watch for breach reports before dispatch.

alerts.title: Himachal ends monsoon with 47 roads still blocked - Mandi 21, Kangra 10, Kullu 7
alerts.summary: Himachal's State Emergency Operations Centre listed 47 roads still blocked statewide on 22 September - Mandi 21, Kangra 10, Kullu 7, Sirmaur and Una 3 each, Lahaul-Spiti 2 and Shimla 1. The count has fallen steadily from 60 on 18 September, so the network is slowly recovering. The 85-day monsoon window from 30 June to 22 September closed with 354 deaths and damage above Rs 3,219 crore, with 601 houses fully destroyed and 1,416 partially damaged.
alerts.impact: Mandi and Kullu remain the binding constraint on Himachal hill line-haul - keep relaxed SLAs on Mandi, Kullu and Kangra rural pincodes but begin restoring normal cut-offs as the blocked count falls. Rebuild FM pickup slots into Kangra first, where the road count is improving fastest.

alerts.title: Himachal Pradesh: Manikaran-Barshaini road (Parvati Valley, Kullu) still not confirmed cleared — repeat slides at Ghatigad keep damaging vehicles
alerts.summary: A large landslide blocked the Manikaran-Barshaini road in Kullu district's Parvati Valley, stranding travellers and cutting connectivity to upper-valley villages including Kasol and Barshaini. The stretch remains volatile — a subsequent slide at Ghatigad damaged another car days later — and no source confirms full restoration as of Sep 22.
alerts.impact: Flag Parvati Valley (Manikaran-Barshaini-Kasol) pincodes non-serviceable for LM/FM until the road is confirmed cleared; route via alternate Kullu-valley approaches where available.

alerts.title: J&K: Doda-Bhaderwah road still blocked at Chalnai village after Sep 19 landslide, no reopening confirmed
alerts.summary: The Doda-Bhaderwah road remains blocked near Chalnai village after a landslide on September 19 halted vehicular movement between the two towns. Debris-clearance machinery remains engaged, but no source confirms full restoration as of Sep 22 — treat the road as still disrupted.
alerts.impact: Route watch — Doda-Bhaderwah corridor: hold non-essential LM/linehaul via Chalnai until the road is confirmed cleared, and route via alternate approach roads where available for Bhaderwah-side pincodes.

alerts.title: NH-44 Jammu-Srinagar open but slow: single-lane chokepoints at Dhalwal and Marog-Nachil Pather
alerts.summary: Per the Sep 28 highway advisory, NH-44 is running two-way (weather permitting) with light/medium and passenger vehicles allowed; persistent single-lane restrictions remain at Dawal (Udhampur) and Marnog-Kishtwar Pather, plus a daytime-only (0700-1800) Heavy Motor Vehicle restriction on the Digdol-Kishani Nallah axis near Ramban-Banihal. Night travel through Ramban-Banihal is still discouraged due to shooting-stone/landslide risk.
alerts.impact: Schedule heavy-vehicle movement on NH-44 within the 0700-1800 window at Digdol-Kishani Nallah and avoid night dispatches through Ramban-Banihal; continue to expect single-lane delays at Dawal and Marnog-Kishtwar Pather.

alerts.title: Pithoragarh-Tanakpur NH-9 at Ghat bend: one-way traffic resumes amid continued rockfall; 11 Pithoragarh roads shut, Adi Kailash Yatra halted
alerts.summary: Ghat bend traffic is being cautiously allowed one-way (as of Sep 25) despite continued stone-fall; NHAI has now sanctioned a Rs 33-crore permanent slope-treatment project (announced Sep 28), confirming intermittent single-lane halts will continue for the near term. Separately, wider Pithoragarh district saw 11 roads closed and the Adi Kailash Yatra halted by heavy rain on Sep 26 (see new alert).
alerts.impact: Continue routing Tanakpur-Pithoragarh consignments with buffer time for cautious one-way movement at Ghat bend; do not expect resolution soon given the multi-month slope-treatment timeline just announced.

alerts.title: UP floods: 12 villages under water in Gonda's Tarabganj & Karnalganj, 54 in Varanasi, 45 in Gorakhpur
alerts.summary: Flooding has worsened with a fresh, ex-Cyclone Arnab-linked rain spell: UP received up to 19x normal rainfall in 24 hours on Sep 26, killing 10 and injuring 17 statewide in rain-related incidents, including 6 deaths across Lakhimpur Kheri, Amethi and Barabanki. Gonda continues to see villages inundated by the Saryu/Ghaghra rivers. IMD expects easing from Sep 29.
alerts.impact: Maintain non-serviceable flags for low-lying Gonda/Lakhimpur Kheri/Amethi/Barabanki pincodes through Sep 28-29; pre-position buffer stock at unaffected UP hubs (Lucknow, Bareilly) for dispatch once roads dry out.

alerts.title: Brent slips below $100 to ~$98 on Iran's Hormuz reopening offer; pump prices unchanged, commercial LPG Rs 2,747.50
alerts.summary: Oil fell about 3% after Iran offered to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days if the US eases pressure, taking Brent below $100 to around $98 a barrel and WTI to about $91. Indian pump prices have not yet moved. Brent crude is trading near $102 a barrel amid Strait of Hormuz shipping disruption. Pump prices held steady again on 23 September: Delhi petrol Rs 102.12 and diesel Rs 95.20, Mumbai Rs 111.21 and Rs 97.83, Chennai Rs 107.76 and Rs 99.55, Bengaluru Rs 110.82 and Rs 98.78, and Hyderabad Rs 115.69 and Rs 103.82 - the costliest metro for both fuels. The 19-kg commercial LPG cylinder is at Rs 2,747.50 in Delhi, up Rs 669 (32.2%) since April, and Rs 2,831.00 in Bengaluru; domestic 14.2-kg LPG is Rs 942 in Delhi. CNG stands at Rs 86.98/kg in Delhi, Rs 88 in Mumbai, Rs 97 in Bengaluru, Rs 112 in Hyderabad, Rs 97.50 in Chennai, Rs 94.02 in Ahmedabad and Rs 93.50 in Kolkata.
alerts.impact: Diesel above Rs 95 in Delhi and above Rs 103 in Hyderabad, with crude over $100, keeps upward pressure on 3P per-shipment LM/FM rates - expect Delhivery, Shadowfax and Xpressbees to raise fuel-surcharge asks in the next rate cycle. Hyderabad is now the worst metro on both diesel (Rs 103.82) and CNG (Rs 112/kg), which materially worsens LM economics there versus Delhi and Mumbai; factor this into capacity-expansion cost cases for Telangana pincodes.

alerts.title: Raghuveer Ghat still not open at full capacity; Khed-Satara link under repair and wall work
alerts.summary: Tarun Bharat reports Raghuveer Ghat, the Khed (Ratnagiri) to Satara link, has still not been restored to full traffic capacity, with PWD road repair and protective retaining-wall construction running on a war footing. This follows the early-September landslide in which part of the carriageway caved after cloudburst-like rain, halting two-way traffic, severing 15-20 Satara-side villages and stranding an ST bus. The ghat stays degraded going into the 23-25 September yellow alert that explicitly covers Ratnagiri and Satara Ghat.
alerts.impact: Do not plan Ratnagiri-Satara cross-ghat middle-mile on Raghuveer until a reopening is confirmed; route via Kumbharli or Amba Ghat instead. The 15-20 cut-off Satara-side villages should stay flagged for extended TAT rather than serviceable.

alerts.title: Karnataka: Agumbe Ghat (NH-169A) heavy-vehicle ban stays in force through September 30 on landslide risk
alerts.summary: Movement of heavy vehicles through Agumbe Ghat on NH-169A, the Malpe-Thirthahalli link, remains prohibited until 30 September because of landslide risk from continuous heavy rain, a ban that has run since 15 June. Only light motor vehicles are permitted. Heavy vehicles from Thirthahalli towards Udupi are directed via the Thirthahalli-Nagar-Kundapur-Udupi route. The 24 September red alert for Dakshina Kannada and Udupi makes an extension beyond 30 September likely.
alerts.impact: Route all Udupi and Mangaluru-bound heavy vehicles via Thirthahalli-Nagar-Kundapur and price the extra leg into Malnad middle-mile costs through at least 30 September. With Agumbe shut, Shiradi and Charmadi carry the entire Bengaluru-Mangaluru load and a slide on either is a single point of failure.

alerts.title: Tamil Nadu: fishermen advised off Gulf of Mannar and Comorin Sea as squally winds up to 55 kmph forecast
alerts.summary: Squally winds of 45-55 kmph gusting occasionally to 65 kmph are forecast over the Gulf of Mannar, the adjoining Comorin area and the south Tamil Nadu coast. Permits are not being issued to mechanised boat fishermen at Rameswaram, and the restriction remains in force until further notice as a precaution against rough seas. No withdrawal of the advisory has been reported.
alerts.impact: Ramanathapuram and Thoothukudi coastal FM volume tied to fishing-harbour clusters stays suppressed while permits are withheld. Keep Rameswaram-island pincodes on extended TAT and avoid committing same-day there.

alerts.title: Odisha: villages remain marooned in Sundargarh's Bonai block as Sarasara, Patang bridges near Balang stay submerged
alerts.summary: At least five villages remain marooned in Sundargarh district's Bonai block after the Sarasara and Patang bridges near Balang stayed submerged; no confirmation of bridge clearance has surfaced. Pre-build buffer stock at Rourkela hub given the compounding cyclone landfall expected Sep 23-24.
alerts.impact: Flag Bonai block villages non-serviceable until bridges are confirmed clear; pre-build buffer stock at Rourkela hub given the compounding cyclone landfall on Sep 23-24.

alerts.title: Jharkhand yellow alert for 11 districts on 23 September, orange for five districts on 24 September
alerts.summary: Flooding continues: India Today (Sep27) reports rivers crossing danger marks and six flights cancelled at Ranchi airport due to relentless rain; New Indian Express (Sep26) reports low-lying areas inundated and vehicle movement affected in several districts.
alerts.impact: Ranchi-area air/road disruption compounds ground delivery delays; treat as an ongoing multi-district risk, not isolated to one town.

alerts.title: Jharkhand: Ganga flood in Sahibganj floods Bhartiya Colony, Rasoolpur; Udhwa erosion sweeps away school and homes
alerts.summary: The Ganga is flowing roughly 57cm above the danger mark at Sahibganj, flooding Bhartiya Colony and Rasoolpur localities; separately, erosion in Udhwa block has destroyed homes and a school building in the Ganga diyara belt.
alerts.impact: Flag Sahibganj town (Bhartiya Colony, Rasoolpur) and Udhwa diyara-belt pincodes non-serviceable; verify riverside addresses before LM dispatch and monitor for further erosion through the week.

alerts.title: Padma erosion swallows 19 houses and a Manasa temple at Radhakrishnapur, Taranagar in Raghunathganj II
alerts.summary: Erosion turned severe in the Radhakrishnapur area of Taranagar village in Raghunathganj II block, Murshidabad, taking 19 homes, an old Manasa temple, shops and several bighas of farmland. Another 50 to 70 houses are under immediate threat. The Farakka-belt blocks - Farakka, Samserganj, Suti I and II, Raghunathganj II, Lalgola, Bhagawangola I and II, Raninagar I and II and Jalangi - face this every year.
alerts.impact: Treat Raghunathganj II, Suti and Samserganj riverside pincodes as shrinking serviceable areas and re-verify addresses before dispatch. Route Murshidabad FM through Jangipur town rather than the riverbank villages.

alerts.title: Fresh Ganga erosion in Malda's Manikchak washes away about 50 houses; nine schools suspend classes
alerts.summary: Fresh Ganga erosion in the Manikchak block of Malda washed away around 50 houses and triggered panic among residents. The district administration suspended classes at nine primary schools across the Manikchak and Ratua-I blocks. Irrigation engineers expect erosion to continue to the end of September because of fluctuating Ganga levels, and state ministers inspected flood and erosion-hit stretches in Manikchak and Ratua-I on 19 September.
alerts.impact: Manikchak and Ratua-I pincodes need address re-validation as households relocate, and FM pickup from riverside seller clusters there should be suspended rather than reattempted. Expect continued serviceability loss across Malda through end-September.

alerts.title: Brahmaputra erosion devours Majuli's Bhakat Chapari and Chabua's Balijan; 25 families homeless
alerts.summary: Massive erosion is under way along Bhakat Chapari in Majuli, with the threat now extending to 16 villages and lower Majuli. At Balijan in Chabua a single day's erosion washed away crores' worth of geo-bags and at least 25 families lost homes and farmland. The Water Resources Department is dumping sand-filled geo-bags from boats. Over the decade to 2026, 330 Assam villages have been lost and 23,369 families displaced by erosion, with the Brahmaputra widening 4.64 km at Dhubri.
alerts.impact: Majuli and Chabua address bases are physically shifting - re-validate Majuli, Chabua and Dhubri pincode masters against relocated households before pushing volume, or non-delivery will read as rider failure rather than address loss. Keep Majuli on extended TAT and treat lower-Majuli villages as at risk of permanent serviceability loss.

alerts.title: Rimbi village landslide: 107 evacuated, 30+ homes destroyed; officials say West Sikkim village may be unsafe to inhabit
alerts.summary: Crisis has worsened: EastMojo (Sep 26) reports Rimbi village may become uninhabitable after recurring landslides, with 32+ houses and government quarters damaged; ANI (Sep 26) confirms families shifted to safer locations amid fresh slope movement. Village is under active evacuation/relief operations.
alerts.impact: Avoid routing through Rimbi/Singlitam (West Sikkim, Gyalshing district) entirely; treat as a no-go zone for last-mile delivery until district administration confirms stabilization — this is a settlement-level, not just road-level, disruption.

alerts.title: Haryana rice millers boycott CMR registration before 1 October procurement; 6.5 lakh MT stuck
alerts.summary: Dispute remains unresolved ahead of the Oct 1 procurement start: an estimated 6.5 lakh MT of custom-milled rice is stuck across Haryana with millers still refusing to register for the new season over pending CMR dues (~Rs 2,800 crore) and policy disagreements.
alerts.impact: No change — continue to flag potential paddy/rice-linked logistics congestion at Haryana mandi-adjacent hubs from Oct 1 if the registration standoff is not resolved before procurement begins.

alerts.title: Sharda river erosion swallows nine houses in Lakhimpur Kheri; 20 more at risk, villagers self-demolishing
alerts.summary: Erosion has spread beyond the original site: as of Sep 24, the Mohana river has eaten roughly a metre into paddy fields at Pohari Baba (Tikunia), and the Sharda river is now within 10 metres of farmland at Bajhera (Kunwarpur Kalan); district officials have referred both sites to irrigation authorities for survey and compensation.
alerts.impact: Flag Tikunia and Kunwarpur Kalan-area delivery points for possible access-road subsidence; monitor for further village-level erosion reports before routing FM riders through riverside link roads.

alerts.title: Nhava Sheva/JNPA congestion persists; gate-in turnaround near 20 hours for some truckers
alerts.summary: Congestion at JNPT/Nhava Sheva continues. Trade bodies report the disruption is being driven by an APMT (BMCT) berth closure for infrastructure upgrades that has diverted vessel and cargo traffic to other terminals (e.g. PSA Mumbai/NSICT), causing landside logjams; the Container Freight Stations Association of India (CFSAI) has attributed continued operational delays at JNPA-linked CFS facilities to this traffic congestion and infrastructure constraints.
alerts.impact: Continue building extra buffer time (~20 hrs) for gate-in/gate-out at JNPT-linked CFS/ICDs; where possible, route FM pickups tied to import consignments via CFS facilities with shorter current queues and monitor JNPA/CFSAI advisories for terminal-specific delays.

alerts.title: Marathwada drought protests: Dharashiv farmers block the Dhule-Solapur highway at Yedshi
alerts.summary: Maharashtra's government officially declared drought in 265 of 358 talukas (Sep 26, 2026) -- including nearly all of Marathwada -- and announced relief measures for farmers, students and rural households, following sustained protests such as the Dharashiv farmers' blockade of the Dhule-Solapur highway (NH-52) over scorched soybean crops.
alerts.impact: The official declaration may ease the most acute protest activity short-term, but sporadic rasta roko/tractor-march actions remain likely in Dharashiv, Beed, Latur and other Marathwada talukas as relief disbursement is monitored; keep contingency routing for the Dhule-Solapur (NH-52) corridor through Dharashiv.

alerts.title: Monsoon retreating: withdrawal line at Jaisalmer-Nagaur-Sikar, Saurashtra-Kutch dry in three to four days
alerts.summary: Monsoon withdrawal continues across western Rajasthan, with Barmer and Jaisalmer recording high temperatures (~43-44C) as dry, post-withdrawal conditions set in; IMD forecasts rain returning to eastern Rajasthan districts from Sep 27 as the withdrawal line shifts further east. Separately, Gujarat's Saurashtra-Kutch and South Gujarat regions are forecast to get a fresh rain spell around Sep 30-Oct 1, suggesting a short lull before the next system.
alerts.impact: Expect a near-term lull in monsoon-related disruption in western Rajasthan and Saurashtra-Kutch, but plan for a fresh Gujarat rain spell (Saurashtra-Kutch to South Gujarat) affecting collection/delivery routes from around Sep 30.

alerts.title: East MP heavy rain from Sep 24: Chhatarpur, Panna, Satna, Shahdol, Mandla, Balaghat, Seoni, Chhindwara; peak Sep 25-26
alerts.summary: The forecast heavy-rain spell over eastern MP (Chhatarpur, Panna, Satna, Shahdol, Mandla etc.) materialized and was reinforced around Sep 26 by remnants of Cyclone Arnab (Bay of Bengal), which triggered a fresh 'very heavy rain' alert across 13 MP districts. State-wide seasonal rainfall has now reached roughly 95.4% of normal with 25 districts recording their full quota, indicating the monsoon is in its final active phase but still capable of sharp spells.
alerts.impact: Relax SLAs for eastern MP rural pincodes (Mandla, Dindori, Balaghat, Seoni, Shahdol) for 25-26 September and route Jabalpur-bound line-haul in daylight. West MP (Indore, Bhopal, Ujjain) should run near normal.

alerts.title: Cyclone Arnab (deep depression) weakens to low-pressure area over Chhattisgarh after Odisha-AP landfall
alerts.summary: The Bay of Bengal system publicly tracked as 'Cyclone Arnab' made landfall as a deep depression near Kalingapatnam, between Visakhapatnam and Gopalpur, around midnight Sep 23-24. It crossed into south interior Odisha (near Nuapada) by Sep 25 and has since weakened further into a well-marked low-pressure area tracking north-northwest toward Chhattisgarh and Madhya Pradesh. Over 8,000 people were evacuated across Odisha and Andhra Pradesh during the landfall phase, with heavy rain also reported in Jharkhand.
alerts.impact: Vizag, Gopalpur, Kalingapatnam and south Odisha/north AP hubs saw LM/FM stoppages during landfall (Sep 23-25); those should be largely clear now. Watch for a secondary rain band over Chhattisgarh (Raipur/Bastar belt) and Madhya Pradesh over the next 24-48h - keep buffer stock and SLA relaxation flags active for those hubs rather than the coast.

alerts.title: Red alert for Srikakulam, Vizianagaram and Parvathipuram Manyam; extremely heavy rain 23-24 September
alerts.summary: Srikakulam, Vizianagaram and Parvathipuram Manyam are under red alert for extremely heavy rain on 22-23 September, with the downpour peaking again on 23-24 September across those districts plus Alluri Sitharama Raju. District officials are on high alert and holidays have been declared. One death was reported: M. Hemantha Krishna of Vijayawada drowned in the overflowing Thotapalli canal at Seethanagaram mandal, Parvathipuram Manyam district. An orange alert for 24 September covers Kakinada, Konaseema, East and West Godavari and Eluru, with Visakhapatnam, Anakapalle, Krishna, Guntur, NTR and Bapatla on yellow. NDRF has five teams at Visakhapatnam, Srikakulam, Vizianagaram and Yanam.
alerts.impact: Flag Srikakulam, Vizianagaram, Parvathipuram Manyam and Alluri Sitharama Raju rural pincodes non-serviceable for 23-24 September and hold the Godavari delta - Kakinada, Konaseema, Eluru - on extended TAT for the 24th. Pause Vizag hub outbound overnight and restart only after the system clears inland.

alerts.title: South Chhattisgarh braces for extremely heavy rain on 24 September; Bastar, Bijapur, Sukma flagged
alerts.summary: With the weakening deep depression tracking from south Odisha into Chhattisgarh, the state is under an extremely-heavy-rain warning for 24 Sep and very-heavy-rain warnings for 25 and 26 Sep, with thundersqualls of 50-60 kmph gusting to 70 kmph. South Chhattisgarh — Bastar, Dantewada, Sukma and Bijapur — is expected to see heavy to very heavy rain at some places; residents of low-lying areas have been told to watch for rising streams and waterlogging.
alerts.impact: Treat Bastar-division pincodes (Jagdalpur, Dantewada, Sukma, Bijapur, Narayanpur) as high-risk for LM on 25-26 Sep — interior nala crossings go under quickly; keep COD/RTO buffers and inform carriers of possible NH-30/NH-63 slowdowns. Raipur–Durg–Bilaspur FM hubs may see thunderstorm-related delays.

alerts.title: Bihar: orange alert in 19 districts, yellow in 19 more as depression remnant brings rain Sep 24-26
alerts.summary: Alert has evolved from a 19-district orange warning to a 12-district yellow alert as of Sep28 (ETV Bharat Hindi): Samastipur, Siwan, Saran, Vaishali, Madhubani, Darbhanga, Sheohar, West Champaran, East Champaran, Gopalganj, Sitamarhi and Muzaffarpur, with winds up to 30 km/h. Gandak and Kosi rivers remain swollen from continuous rain in Nepal's terai, and villages across roughly 17 districts have seen submersion.
alerts.impact: Flood risk from Kosi/Gandak persists in north Bihar even as the rain-alert severity itself has eased; continue routing around low-lying embankment-adjacent villages in the 12 alerted districts.

alerts.title: Cloudburst-type downpours hit Poonjar, Erattupetta, Vagamon and Vattavada; 10 dead, high ranges cut
alerts.summary: Extremely intense localised convective downpours - described as cloudburst-like rather than monsoon-trough driven - battered Poonjar, Erattupetta, Vagamon, Kuttikkanam and Vattavada near Munnar on 22 September, triggering widespread landslides. Regina Johnny and her son Josephine Johnny died when their house at Poonjar Payyanithottam collapsed, and soil and gravel blocked the Poonjar-Adivaram road at Peringulam. Total deaths across Malappuram, Kottayam and Idukki reached 10. Idukki's minister-in-charge Anoop Jacob asked travellers to postpone all non-essential travel to the high ranges, with relief camps opened at Pazhampillichal Government LP School and the LP School at Palisakkallu.
alerts.impact: Treat Idukki and eastern Kottayam high-range pincodes - Poonjar, Erattupetta, Vagamon, Kuttikkanam, Munnar and Vattavada - as non-serviceable or extended-TAT until roads are confirmed clear. Because the pattern is cloudburst-driven, forecast alerts will not reliably precede the blockage, so hold buffer stock at Kottayam and Thodupuzha rather than pushing daily into the hills.

alerts.title: Bengaluru IT corridor waterlogged at Marathahalli, KR Puram and Kadubeesanahalli after a second day of rain
alerts.summary: A second consecutive day of heavy showers on 22 September caused severe traffic, waterlogging and tree falls across Bengaluru. Water accumulated at Thubarahalli, Varthur Kodi, the BGS Flyover, Marathahalli, Kadubeesanahalli and KR Puram, all on the eastern IT corridor. The city observatory logged 15.9 mm in the 24 hours to 8:30 am and traffic police advised alternative routes.
alerts.impact: Bengaluru east LM - Whitefield, Marathahalli, Bellandur, KR Puram and Varthur pincodes - will run 60 to 90 minutes behind on rain evenings, so shift those beats earlier and re-sequence around Varthur Kodi and the BGS flyover. Move FM pickups from Whitefield seller clusters into morning slots.

alerts.title: Dikchu-Mangan road cut at Zin Khola and 5th Mile; even transhipment is not possible
alerts.summary: Major landslides at Zin Khola and 5th Mile have completely halted travel between Dikchu and Mangan in North Sikkim, and transhipment - walking goods across the slide to a waiting vehicle - is not possible at Zin Khola. Clearance crews were waiting for rain to abate before deploying heavy machinery. This is a second North Sikkim connectivity failure alongside the NH-10 Bardang restriction.
alerts.impact: Mangan and North Sikkim pincodes should be flagged non-serviceable rather than extended-TAT, because no transhipment workaround exists at Zin Khola. Stop accepting new North Sikkim orders until a reopening is confirmed.

alerts.title: NH-29 Kohima-Dimapur degraded: one side blocked at Sechu Zubza, seven points fully blocked
alerts.summary: NH-29 Dimapur-Kohima is reported open to traffic but still vulnerable, with round-the-clock patrols active per Eastern Mirror Nagaland ('NH-29 open but vulnerable, round-the-clock patrols active'); slope protection works remain incomplete. Road is passable but conditions can deteriorate quickly with further rain.
alerts.impact: Dimapur-Kohima is Nagaland's main freight artery and is now single-carriageway at multiple points - add two to three hours per run and route per the police diversions. This also degrades Dimapur as a staging option for Manipur-bound volume held back by the UNC blockade.

alerts.title: UFBU 3-day nationwide bank strike Sep 28-30; branches effectively shut for five days from Sep 26
alerts.summary: The United Forum of Bank Unions' three-day nationwide strike began today, 28 September, after conciliation before the Deputy Chief Labour Commissioner remained inconclusive; the core demand is a five-day banking week. Branches have been effectively unavailable for normal customer-facing work for five consecutive days counting the preceding weekend (26-30 September). SBI and other PSBs have advised customers to rely on ATMs, Customer Service Points, internet banking, YONO, mobile banking and UPI through 30 September. Unions have warned of an indefinite nationwide strike from 26 October if the dispute remains unresolved.
alerts.impact: COD remittance, cash deposit and branch-dependent settlement cycles for Delhivery, Shadowfax and Xpressbees delivery partners will stall from 26 to 30 Sep - pre-fund partner float and move DP payouts to digital rails before 25 Sep. Expect cash-handling friction at rural CSP-dependent LM hubs; the window also overlaps month-end, so clear vendor payments and FM pickup-agent settlements ahead of it.

sources.name: NewsX - Bank Strike 2026, 3-day nationwide strike from Sept 28 (ground report, TV)

alerts.title: Alluri Sitharama Raju agency: night heavy-vehicle ban on ghat roads; KK-line express trains halted Sep 23-24
alerts.summary: Police have restricted night movement of heavy vehicles on ghat roads in the agency areas of Alluri Sitharama Raju district because of landslide risk from the deep depression's rainfall. East Coast Railway has suspended several express services on the Visakhapatnam-Kottavalasa-Kirandul (KK) line on 23 and 24 September. Vizianagaram district has declared a school holiday for 23 September on the collector's orders. Red alerts are in force for Srikakulam, Parvathipuram Manyam and Vizianagaram, orange for Visakhapatnam, Anakapalli and Alluri Sitharama Raju, and yellow for Kakinada, Eluru, the combined Godavari districts and Krishna. Officials have warned that road transport and even helicopter services may have to be curtailed.
alerts.impact: Do not schedule overnight line-haul on the Araku, Chintapalli, Paderu or Rampachodavaram ghat sections until 25 Sep. Rail-fed FM/LM legs in Vizianagaram, Parvathipuram Manyam and Alluri districts lose the KK-line feed for two days - shift to road only where the ghat ban allows, and pre-flag Araku and Paderu tribal-belt pincodes as extended-SLA or temporarily non-serviceable.

alerts.title: Assam: Brahmaputra swallows much of Roumari Pathar village in Barpeta; Barkhetri residents on night watch
alerts.summary: Severe erosion has continued for nearly a month at Roumari Pathar in Barpeta district, where the Brahmaputra has reportedly swallowed a major portion of the village along with public institutions, farmland and the homesteads of hundreds of families. Riverbank erosion along the Brahmaputra is also keeping residents of Barkhetri awake at night. Statewide, erosion by the Brahmaputra and its tributaries has wiped out close to 330 villages over a decade and affected 23,369 families between 2016 and 2026, with Dhubri worst hit at 5,241 families and the river widening there by 4.64 km; Morigaon, South Salmara-Mankachar and Barpeta are the other hardest-hit districts.
alerts.impact: Retire address masters for eroded habitations in Roumari Pathar and the Barkhetri belt rather than carrying them as repeat failed-attempt pincodes - this is a structural serviceability loss, not a weather event. Rebase Barpeta, Dhubri, Morigaon and South Salmara LM beat plans on surviving villages, and avoid siting new 3P last-mile touchpoints inside the active erosion corridor.

alerts.title: Himachal: fresh slide halts Chailchowk-Tattapani road in Mandi; Chandigarh-Manali highway back to one-way
alerts.summary: A fresh landslide stopped traffic for three hours on the Chailchowk-Tattapani road in Mandi district. Officials counted 60 blocked roads statewide that day, with Mandi worst hit at 33, followed by Kangra at 10 and Kullu at nine. Feeder stretches toward Kullu have seen episodic slides through the month, adding unpredictability to transit times. A separate 24-hour landslide block on the Chandigarh-Manali highway has since been cleared to one-way traffic. The weather office expects light rain with isolated showers in the middle hills.
alerts.impact: Build a 12-24 hour buffer into Mandi and Kullu LM promise dates - the Chailchowk, Karsog and Tattapani belt pincodes are the most exposed. Send Manali-bound line-haul only in daylight while the Chandigarh-Manali highway runs one-way, and hold off on new 3P LM expansion in interior Mandi until the monsoon fully withdraws.

alerts.title: Gajapati keeps 140 identified landslide-prone spots under watch; 6 cyclone and 264 temporary shelters readied
alerts.summary: Rain intensified across Gajapati district through 22 September after overnight drizzle, and a red warning is in force for the district. The administration is keeping a special watch on 140 identified landslide-prone locations and has directed BDOs and tehsildars of every block to monitor and act immediately. Six cyclone shelters and 264 temporary shelters have been readied, and the Fire Services Department is on alert for uprooted trees and blocked roads. The District Fire Officer said rescue teams were pre-positioned a week in advance on the strength of the red warning.
alerts.impact: Gajapati's ghat pincodes - Mohana, Nuagada, R Udayagiri and the Paralakhemundi-Berhampur approach - should be treated as landslide-interruptible rather than merely wet: a slide can close a beat with no forecast lead time. Hold Paralakhemundi LM attempts on 23-24 September, stage stock at Berhampur, and expect FM pickup loss across the district's interior blocks.

alerts.title: Red warning continues for Nabarangpur, Kalahandi, Koraput as south Odisha depression weakens but rain persists
alerts.summary: The deep depression over south Odisha that triggered the red warning has weakened into a depression and is moving towards Chhattisgarh (Pragativadi, OdishaBytes reports, Sep26-27), easing the most severe rain threat over Nabarangpur, Kalahandi and Koraput though heavy rain and road-cut risk persists in the ghat belt.
alerts.impact: Maintain non-serviceable/extended-SLA flags for interior blocks of Nabarangpur, Kalahandi and Koraput districts through the red-warning window; avoid committing tight linehaul schedules on ghat and interior roads in this belt until the warning is downgraded.

alerts.title: Konkan and Goa under widespread rain with thunderstorms and gusty winds on 23 September
alerts.summary: IMD's outlook for 23 September puts widespread rainfall over Konkan and Goa with heavy showers likely at isolated places, accompanied by thunderstorms, lightning and gusty winds. The spell lands inside the Ganeshotsav immersion window, when NH-66 is already closed to trucks of 16 tonnes and above and Mumbai and Pune have their own heavy-vehicle bans in force.
alerts.impact: Panaji, Margao, Mapusa and Ponda LM should carry a half-day weather buffer on 23-24 September, and Ratnagiri-Sindhudurg beats already routed off NH-66 have almost no slack left. Do not commit same-day in coastal Goa while thunderstorm and gusty-wind conditions persist.

alerts.title: Vizianagaram: Chandrampeta–Vasantha road shut as Ginjerugedda stream floods; Palasa, Kalingapatnam log ~10 cm
alerts.summary: Officials suspended traffic on the Chandrampeta–Vasantha road in Vizianagaram district after heavy water from the Ginjerugedda stream flooded it following rain since Monday night. APSDMA recorded about 10 cm at Palasa and Kalingapatnam (Srikakulam), 7.1 cm at Peda Bayalu (Alluri Sitarama Raju) and 6.2 cm at Bhogapuram (Vizianagaram). IMD-Amaravati issued an orange alert for 24 Sep for Parvathipuram Manyam, ASR, Kakinada, Konaseema, East/West Godavari and Eluru, with a yellow alert for Srikakulam, Vizianagaram, Visakhapatnam, Anakapalle, Krishna, Guntur, NTR and Bapatla. Update: local reports on 26 Sep say floodwaters in the Gantyada/Gedda Vagu stream stretch have receded and road access is being restored, though residual waterlogging may persist in low spots.
alerts.impact: Downgrade from non-serviceable to extended-SLA watch for Chandrampeta-Vasantha (Vizianagaram) as floodwaters recede; confirm road passability before resuming normal LM cut-offs.

alerts.title: Saurashtra: rain across 93 talukas — Mahuva 4 in, Gondal 3.6 in, Manavadar 3 in ahead of monsoon withdrawal
alerts.summary: Rain fell across 93 talukas of Gujarat in 24 hours, mostly in Saurashtra. Mahuva (Bhavnagar) had the most at 4 inches, followed by Gondal (Rajkot) at 3.62 inches, Manavadar 3 inches, Junagadh city 2.36 inches, and Vanthali, Veraval and Bhanvad about 2 inches each. Keshod and Vadia recorded about 1.7–1.8 inches.
alerts.impact: Localized waterlogging risk only; no route closures reported. Watch LM TAT on Mahuva, Gondal, Junagadh, Veraval and Keshod beats (Rajkot/Junagadh/Bhavnagar hubs) for short delays. No non-serviceable flags needed for now.

alerts.title: Srikakulam: Palasa 14 cm, Sompeta 13 cm, Tekkali 11 cm; water enters homes at Tekkali's Bhavani Nagar
alerts.summary: IMD said Palasa in Srikakulam district recorded 14 cm on 23 September, the state's highest, followed by Sompeta (13 cm), Kalingapatnam (12 cm), Tekkali (11 cm) and Araku Valley (10 cm). Incessant rain inundated agricultural fields, low-lying areas and roads at several places in Srikakulam district; rainwater entered homes at Bhavani Nagar in Tekkali and a tree was uprooted in Neelapuram mandal. IMD has a red alert for extremely heavy rain in Srikakulam, Vizianagaram, Parvathipuram Manyam and Alluri Sitarama Raju districts until 8:30 am on 24 September, and flags extremely heavy rain again over Eluru and ASR from 24 to 25 September. The state expects heavy rain in 129 mandals and extremely heavy rain in nine.
alerts.impact: Treat the Palasa–Sompeta–Tekkali belt (Srikakulam's northern beats on the NH-16 corridor toward Odisha) as partly non-serviceable on 23–24 September: hold LM attempts in low-lying Tekkali wards, stagger FM pickups, and route Srikakulam-bound line-haul only after the landfall squalls pass. Pre-alert Eluru and Araku/Paderu (ASR) hubs for the second extreme-rain window on 24–25 September.

alerts.title: Idukki bans night travel (7 pm–6 am) in hill areas; Munnar town traffic diverted, Adimali Pazhampillichal families shifted
alerts.summary: The Idukki district administration has banned all night travel in high-range areas from 7 pm to 6 am and shut adventure-tourism spots until rain alerts are withdrawn. In Munnar, vehicles from Old Munnar to the town are diverted via the Gap Road near the CSI church and the bridge by the police station. Families at landslide risk in Adimali's Pazhampillichal were evacuated, fallen trees blocked the Kochi–Dhanushkodi national highway at several points, and travellers on the Neriamangalam–Valara stretch were told to take extreme care. On 22 September, landslides briefly cut the Erattupetta–Vagamon road, damaged the Poonjar–Adivaram road at several points, and cut off about 30 families and tourists at Thattambara near Vattavada; Idukki's minister-in-charge asked tourists to postpone non-essential travel to the high ranges.
alerts.impact: Night line-haul into Idukki is effectively closed. Push Munnar, Adimali, Kattappana and Nedumkandam dispatches out of Kochi/Muvattupuzha in the morning so vans clear the ghat before 7 pm, and add a D+1 buffer for Vagamon, Vattavada and the Poonjar–Erattupetta belt. Mark Thattambara/Kottakamboor pincodes non-serviceable until the washed-out roads reopen.

alerts.title: Wayanad collector halts quarrying, trekking near Mundakkai-Chooralmala (Meppadi) as rain alert renews landslide vigil
alerts.summary: With IMD issuing a yellow alert for 7-12 cm of rain, the Wayanad district collector ordered a halt to granite quarrying, adventure-tourism operations and trekking, directing authorities to closely monitor earth-slip-prone zones. Special vigilance was flagged for the Mundakkai-Chooralmala area of Meppadi panchayat - site of the July 2024 landslide that killed dozens - along with the Kalladi-Anakkampoyil tunnel site and the Wayanad Township project near Kalpetta.
alerts.impact: Treat Meppadi, Mundakkai, Chooralmala and the Kalpetta hill belt as elevated-risk for LM/FM through this rain spell; avoid dispatching riders on hill roads after dark, and pre-position Meppadi-bound stock at the Kalpetta hub in case local roads are closed on short notice.

alerts.title: Saharsa: Kosi floodwater enters Kedli, Rampur, Barhara villages between embankments as Birpur discharges season's peak 3.13 lakh cusecs
alerts.summary: The Kosi river has swelled to its highest discharge of the season, with the Birpur barrage recording 3.13 lakh cusecs on 26-27 September. Floodwater has entered homes and kitchens in Kedli (near the eastern Kosi embankment), Rampur, Barhara and other villages lying between the eastern and western Kosi embankments in Saharsa district. Roads in these villages are now largely unusable, with boats - often overloaded with 20-25 people - the only way in or out as currents strengthen. Families are also short of drinking water, firewood and livestock fodder; the administration has urged evacuation to higher ground but many residents are staying back to protect homes and animals.
alerts.impact: Flag Kedli, Rampur, Barhara and other between-embankment villages in Saharsa district as non-serviceable for LM/FM - roads are impassable and only limited boat transport is available. Hold FM pickups from Kosi-belt sellers in Saharsa and add a multi-day SLA buffer until the Birpur discharge recedes from its seasonal peak.

alerts.title: Kani river overflow submerges two panchayats in Jajpur's Dasarathpur block, Odisha
alerts.summary: Situation has escalated: Sambad English/OdishaTV report a fresh ~70-foot breach in the Kani river embankment (this is the fifth flood in Dasarathpur block in 50 days), and as of Sep28, Jajpur district ordered 91 primary schools shut across Dasarathpur, Jajpur and Binjharpur blocks due to flooding (Kalinga TV).
alerts.impact: Recurring embankment failures mean this is not a one-off; treat Dasarathpur/Jajpur block roads as a standing risk for repeat cut-offs, not a single resolved incident.

alerts.title: Similipal's Devkund access route cut as bridges/culverts washed away, Mayurbhanj
alerts.summary: Heavy rainfall has washed away or damaged bridges and culverts on the access route to the Devkund tourist site inside Similipal National Park, Mayurbhanj district, prompting a temporary closure of the site. The area sits within the wider Odisha flood emergency affecting Balasore, Jajpur, Koraput and Kalahandi districts.
alerts.impact: Low direct LM/FM impact (forest/tourism route), but signals continued road-infrastructure damage in Mayurbhanj's interior blocks - worth a spot-check on any last-mile roads feeding villages near Similimal's buffer zone before committing delivery SLAs there this week.

alerts.title: Heavy rain shuts 11 roads across Pithoragarh district, halts Adi Kailash Yatra route
alerts.summary: Heavy rainfall across Pithoragarh district on Sep 26 forced closure of 11 roads district-wide and halted the Adi Kailash Yatra pilgrimage route, in addition to the separately tracked chronic Ghat bend chokepoint on NH-9. NHAI has now sanctioned a Rs 33-crore permanent slope-treatment project at Ghat bend (announced Sep 28), confirming disruption at that spot is expected to persist near-term even as fresh closures hit other roads in the district.
alerts.impact: Expect delivery delays and possible non-serviceable flags across multiple Pithoragarh district pincodes beyond the NH-9 Ghat bend stretch already tracked separately; stage buffer stock at Tanakpur/Haldwani hubs for onward dispatch once district roads reopen, and add a 1-2 day SLA buffer for last-mile in hill-block pincodes.

alerts.title: Maharashtra declares drought in 265 of 358 talukas, nearly all of Marathwada covered
alerts.summary: The Maharashtra government officially declared drought conditions in 265 of the state's 358 talukas (about 74%) on Sep 26, 2026, after a weak monsoon caused widespread crop losses, with nearly all of Marathwada included. Relief measures for farmers, students and rural households were announced alongside the declaration.
alerts.impact: Farmer distress remains high in Marathwada and other drought-hit talukas; expect continued sporadic rasta roko/tractor-march protests on rural arterial roads (notably the NH-52 Dhule-Solapur corridor through Dharashiv) as relief rollout is monitored. LM/FM teams should keep contingency routing and extra buffer time for routes through Dharashiv, Beed, Latur and Akola belts.

alerts.title: Kerala coast under Kallakkadal high-wave warning alongside yellow rain alert statewide
alerts.summary: IMD has issued a yellow rain alert along with an active Kallakkadal (sudden sea-incursion/high-wave) warning for Kerala's coast as of Sep 28, following the easing of the statewide orange alert. Low-lying coastal roads and fishing harbour approach roads are at risk of sudden wave surge and localized flooding.
alerts.impact: Coastal LM routes near harbours and low-lying beach-adjacent roads in Kerala should be checked for sudden wave-surge flooding before dispatch; minor delays possible on coastal delivery routes during high tide windows.

alerts.title: Landslide between Maligura-Chhatariput stations halts Rayagada rail line, trains cancelled through Sep 29
alerts.summary: A landslide between Maligura and Chhatariput stations on the Rayagada Division (Visakhapatnam-Koraput-Jagdalpur line) has forced East Coast Railway to cancel multiple passenger and express trains (including the Kirandul-Visakhapatnam and Rourkela-Jagdalpur services) and short-terminate/short-originate several Howrah-Jagdalpur and Bhubaneswar-Jagdalpur expresses at Koraput. Disruption is scheduled through September 29.
alerts.impact: Any rail-dependent line-haul or parcel movement on the Koraput-Rayagada-Vizag rail corridor will face delays or need road diversion through Sep 29; plan alternate road routing via NH-26/NH-326 for shipments transiting this south Odisha rail corridor.

alerts.title: 341 schools shut in Bhadrak's Bhandaripokhari, Dhamnagar, Tihidi and Chandbali blocks as flood situation persists
alerts.summary: Bhadrak district administration ordered 341 schools closed across Bhandaripokhari, Dhamnagar, Tihidi and Chandbali blocks on Sep 28 due to the ongoing flood situation, alongside 91 schools shut in neighbouring Jajpur's Dasarathpur, Jajpur and Binjharpur blocks.
alerts.impact: Expect localized road access issues and reduced last-mile activity in these four Bhadrak blocks; treat Bhadrak as a new active flood pocket distinct from the already-tracked Jajpur/Kani river breach.

alerts.title: Rushikulya river rises in Ganjam, floodwater enters villages
alerts.summary: The Rushikulya river's water level continued rising in Ganjam district, with floodwater entering several villages, as part of the broader south Odisha rain system (Kanak News ground report, Sep26). Odisha CM subsequently toured flood-hit districts including Ganjam as the state moved over 1 lakh people to relief camps (PTI, Sep27).
alerts.impact: Watch for village-road access issues in low-lying Rushikulya-belt areas of Ganjam district; coordinate with local hubs before dispatching last-mile runs into riverside villages.
